Wed, 19 Aug 2026 12:12:22 +0000 en-US hourly 1 https://wordpress.org/?v=7.0.4 https://beesayatv.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/cropped-09-32x32.png River Crossing – beesayatv https://beesayatv.com/ 32 32 Guindaruhan-Estaka Trail Loop | Guindaruhan, Minglanilla | 2026 GPX https://beesayatv.com/trails/guindaruhan-estaka-trail-loop-guindaruhan-minglanilla-2026-gpx/ Wed, 15 Jul 2026 13:56:17 +0000 https://beesayatv.com/?post_type=trail&p=793 The Guindaruhan–Estaka Trail Loop is a documented 3.04 km loop hike in Barangay Guindaruhan, Minglanilla. I followed a combination of quiet community roads and established footpaths that descended into the valley of Cutod Falls before returning through Estaka to complete the loop.

The route remained easy to follow throughout, despite sections where vegetation partially covered the trail. I completed this hike in March 2026 under sunny morning conditions.

Trail Snapshot

EASY
DocumentedMarch 2026
Distance3.04 km (Loop)
Duration1.5 - 2 hrs
WaterAt least 1 liter
ShadeLimited
Surface40% trail, 60% road
GPXWikiloc

Forecast data: Open-Meteo

Access

I started near Guindaruhan National High School, where motorcycle parking was available along the roadside without a parking fee. The trailhead was accessible by concrete road, and private vehicles could reach the area. Public transportation was limited, although habal-habal services were available.

Why this trail is rated Easy

✓ Clear and easy-to-follow trail
✓ Frequent communities, farms, or other trail users encountered
✓ No significant cliff exposure or technical terrain
✓ Short hiking distance
✓ Gentle or gradual elevation changes

On this trail: river crossing • waterfall

Route Description

I began by walking along a gradually ascending concrete road through Barangay Guindaruhan before passing the small communities of Purok Cacao. From there, the route left the road and followed a narrow footpath descending toward Cutod Falls. Although dense vegetation covered parts of the trail during my visit, I had no difficulty following the route.

After reaching the waterfalls, I continued through the valley on well-established footpaths that local residents regularly used as a shortcut to Guindaruhan proper. The loop then climbed out through Estaka, where I followed a concrete road past more communities before returning to the starting point.

Trail Conditions

The weather remained sunny throughout my hike. Much of the route had limited shade, while the trail stayed dry during my visit. Mobile signal was strong near the start before becoming intermittent farther along the route. I found stores near the communities, encountered mostly local residents, and noticed many insects. Approximately 40% of the route followed trails, while the remaining 60% used concrete roads.

Additional Notes

The trail around Cutod Falls remained well-defined despite the overgrown vegetation in some sections. I also noticed litter around the waterfalls, even though signs reminding visitors not to leave trash were present.

]]> Camp 8 to Matun-og Falls Hike (Updated) | Camp 8, Guindaruhan-Crasher Site | 2026 GPX https://beesayatv.com/trails/camp-8-to-matun-og-falls-hike-anxiety-took-over-camp-8-minglanilla-2026-gpx/ Sat, 04 Jul 2026 10:38:04 +0000 https://beesayatv.com/?post_type=trail&p=487 The Camp 8 to Matun-og Falls trail is a 5.72-kilometer point-to-point community route in Minglanilla, passing through farms, local settlements, and the valley leading toward Matun-og Falls. I hiked it in August 2026, starting from Camp 8 and approaching the falls from the opposite direction of the more commonly used Guindaruhan–Taboan–Crasher Site route.

Although the distance is relatively short, I dealt with repeated climbs and descents along the way. This was my second attempt from Camp 8, and this time I reached Matun-og Falls.

Trail Snapshot

TOUGH
DocumentedAugust 2026
Distance5.72 km (Point-to-Point)
Duration3 - 3.5 hrs
WaterAt least 2 liters
ShadeLimited
Surface100% trail
GPXWikiloc

Forecast data: Open-Meteo

Access

I parked my motorcycle along the concrete road near the jump-off point, where there was no parking fee. Private vehicles can reach the area, while public transportation is limited. Habal-habal service is also available.

Why this trail is rated Tough

✓ Significant endurance required
✓ Sustained steep ascent or descent
✓ Limited or no mobile signal
✓ Navigation requires attention
✓ Limited bailout options

On this trail: farmland • river crossing • valley

Route Description

From the jump-off point, I immediately started on a short but steep climb toward the top of the mountain. Locals use this trail regularly, so much of the route is well-trodden.

Early in the ascent, I followed a cemented staircase. Some sections were already missing, but the remaining steps made that part of the climb easier.

As I continued, I passed farmland planted with corn and camote. I also saw cows, goats, and a few carabaos along the route.

The trail passes through several local communities, including settlements deeper in the valley. Other sections felt more isolated because dense vegetation blocked much of the surrounding view.

Later, I descended toward the river that feeds Matun-og Falls. That section gave me the most difficulty because of the steep slope and loose surface.

Trail Conditions

The morning was sunny, and it had not rained for several days. I found the trail very dry, with loose soil that became particularly slippery during the descent toward the river. Based on the condition noted for this route, the same trail can become muddy and slippery after rain.

Shade was limited during the hike, and I did not pass any stores along the route. I encountered locals but few insects. Mobile signal was limited or absent in some sections.

There is also a significant section of river trekking before reaching Matun-og Falls. During this hike, the river section was passable, but this part of the route could become dangerous during heavy rain or a sudden rise in water level.

Additional Notes

Most hikers taking this connection travel in the opposite direction, coming from Matun-og Falls and climbing toward Camp 8. On the steep section I descended, climbing would have been easier than going down on the dry, loose soil.

For the exact route I followed, a trekking pole would have helped with the descent. I carried the expectation of needing at least two liters of water because of the limited shade and the repeated climbs and descents.

]]> Cambanog Falls | Dumanjug | 2026 GPX https://beesayatv.com/trails/cambanog-falls-dumanjug-2026-gpx/ Wed, 01 Jul 2026 07:20:43 +0000 https://beesayatv.com/?post_type=trail&p=414 Cambanog Falls is a documented 2 km out-and-back hike in Langin, Kambanog, Dumanjug. I followed a short trail that descended through open terrain toward the river before returning along the same route. Although the approach was mostly downhill, the lower sections included a few uneven areas and short climbs before the continuous uphill walk back to the jump-off. I completed this hike in April 2026.

EASY

Distance~2 km (Out and Back)
Duration15-30 mins
WaterAt least 1 liter

Access

I started near Cambanog Elementary School, where motorcycle parking was available along the roadside without a parking fee. The jump-off was accessible by a rough road, and private vehicles could reach the area. Public transportation was limited, although habal-habal services were available.

Why this trail is rated Easy

✓ Easy-to-follow trail
✓ No technical climbing required
✓ Short hiking distance
✓ Mostly downhill route
✓ River crossings are manageable during normal conditions

On this trail: river crossing • waterfall

Route Description

I began by descending toward the river on a trail that was easy to follow. The upper section gradually lost elevation before reaching a few uneven stretches and short climbs closer to the water. After reaching Cambanog Falls, I retraced the same route back to the starting point.

The return consisted of a steady uphill climb from the river to the jump-off. Even though the overall distance was short, the climb out required more effort than the approach.

Trail Conditions

The weather remained sunny throughout my hike. Most of the route was exposed with limited shade, while the trail stayed dry during my visit. Walking conditions could become muddy after rain. I found a few stores near the route, and mobile signal remained strong near the jump-off before disappearing near the river.

Additional Notes

The trail surface is mostly soil from the jump-off point to the river and can become very muddy after rain.

I began by following farmland trails that gradually climbed across rolling countryside. The route remained easy to follow as it crossed open terrain with gentle to moderate uphill sections. Along the way, I crossed two small rivers before continuing toward the turnaround point.

The second half of the hike gradually shifted into a longer downhill return. Although the terrain never became technical, the sustained descent felt more tiring toward the end of the hike.

Navigation remained simple throughout the hike, making the route easy to follow from start to finish. I completed this hike in May 2026.

]]> Danasan Falls Trail Loop | Danasan, Danao | 2026 GPX https://beesayatv.com/trails/danasan-trail-loop/ Wed, 24 Jun 2026 14:40:34 +0000 https://beesayatv.com/?post_type=trail&p=132 The Danasan Falls Trail Loop is a documented 5.84 km loop hike in Danasan, Danao City. I followed the longer approach before descending to Cantaling Falls, which some maps also label as Danasan Falls, then returned via a sustained uphill climb to complete the loop. The longer route offered gentler terrain before joining the same ascent used by the shorter direct route. I completed this hike in June 2026 under sunny morning conditions.

Trail Snapshot

MILD
DocumentedJune 2026
Distance5.84 km (Loop)
Duration3-4 hrs
WaterAt least 1 liter
ShadeModerate
Surface85% trail, 15% road
GPXWikiloc

Forecast data: Open-Meteo

Access

I started near Danasan Elementary School, where motorcycle parking was available along the roadside without a parking fee. The roads leading to the jump-off included a mix of concrete, paved, and dirt sections. Private vehicles could reach the area, while public transportation was very limited.

Habal-habal services were available, and local fares from Danao City proper to Danasan Elementary School typically ranged from ₱300 to ₱500 per person, with lower fares possible when sharing a ride. The waterfall is about 28 km from Danao City proper, and the trip usually takes around 45 to 60 minutes by motorcycle or private vehicle.

Why this trail is rated Mild

✓ Frequent hikers encountered
✓ Sustained moderate ascent and descent
✓ Steep sections present
✓ Rocky and uneven footing common
✓ River crossings are manageable

On this trail: farmland • river crossing • waterfall

Route Description

I chose the longer loop instead of the shorter direct route to the falls. The trail was easy to follow, and I regularly crossed paths with other hikers throughout the day. After reaching Cantaling Falls, I began the return climb using the same uphill section shared by both routes.

The trail included sustained ascents and descents, along with several rocky and uneven sections underfoot. I also crossed a number of manageable river crossings before continuing back toward the trailhead. The final climb was the most demanding part of the hike and continued steadily until I returned to the starting point.

Trail Conditions

The weather was sunny throughout the morning. I walked through a mix of shaded and exposed sections, while the trail remained dry during my visit. I found stores only near the communities at the beginning of the hike. Mobile signal started out strong but disappeared farther along the route, and insects were minimal. Because this is a popular waterfall trail, I encountered many other hikers during the day.

Additional Notes

When I arrived at the jump-off, several local guides, mostly children and teenagers, approached me and offered guiding services to Cantaling Falls. Their fees were negotiable. The shorter direct route to the waterfall covers about 2 km and is mostly downhill, but it requires a river crossing that can become difficult or inaccessible after heavy rain. I also noticed that some maps and GPX sources identify the waterfall as Danasan Falls, while recent local usage and hiking content commonly refer to it as Cantaling Falls.
